tables.how: The first 31 rows are every row of the federal oversight committee's final Coronavirus Relief Fund data in which the City is the government reporting (the file prints it as “SAN FRANCISCO, CITY & COUNTY OF”): 17 lines with an amount and 14 correction rows that change only the amount spent. The amounts add to $153,823,502.50, which is what the file says the City received. One line of $116,847,245 names no payee; the other 16 lines name 13 organizations for $36,976,257.50. The last row is the City's only project in the Treasury's recovery-grant data, as the latest release (data to 31 March 2026) gives it: $624,817,342, with no payee. Unnamed lines: $741,664,587 of $778,640,844 (95%), the case's $741,664,587 of $778.6 million. Each payee's spent amounts, with the correction rows added in, come to its award.
tables.limits: Reporting in this way was allowed. The Treasury let a government report payments to individuals, which can include its own public-safety payroll, as one total, and money taken as replacement of lost revenue carries no payee reporting at all. A line without a name is therefore not a sign that anything was hidden or misspent; it means the federal record cannot show who was finally paid, and the City's own ledger is where that would be found. The oversight file holds only the City's last cumulative report.

tables.limits: Taking the grant as replacement of lost revenue was a choice the federal rules offered every government, and a project of that kind has no requirement to report who was paid. The case's figure is the last row: the final report's total spending of $25,444,172.89 less 2,211 households times an average of $7,021.01, which leaves $9,920,720. The quarterly workbooks give more than the case had: $19,429,806 of aid to households, $153,093 of housing-stability services and $4,286,754 of administration, $23,869,653 in all to September 2022.
tables.limits: Households that received rent aid are counted in these files and never named, and no list here names one. The administration figure, all of it in one quarter, is 16.4% of the grant; the program allowed up to 10% for administration and housing-stability services together, and whether the figure was later corrected is not in these files. The Treasury accepted the reports and no audit finding on them is on file.

tables.how: A first-round loan could be at most 2.5 times average monthly payroll, so a loan implies yearly payroll of at least the loan divided by 2.5, times 12. That is set against the largest payroll (officers' pay, other salaries, pensions, benefits and payroll taxes) on any tax return collected for the borrower with a year ending by December 2022. Every City payee with a matched first-round loan of $25,000 or more and such a return is listed: 236. The median loan implies 69% of the payroll on the return. 7 imply 1.25 times or more and 4 imply 1.5 times or more, with loans of $12,093,321 together; the widest is Filipino-American Development Foundation, whose $385,801 loan implies $1,851,844 against $792,725. The multiple is rounded to one decimal place before it is compared with 1.5, as the case does.
tables.limits: The loan was sized on payroll of 2019 or early 2020 and the earliest returns on file end in 2020, so an organization that shrank in 2020 shows a gap honestly. Housing and arts groups often employ staff through affiliates that file their own returns, and pay above $100,000 a person did not count toward the loan. Every loan was approved by a lender and most were forgiven by the Small Business Administration: a high multiple is a question for the borrower. Loans are tied to payees by name. A tax return is the organization's own statement, signed under penalty of perjury and not audited by the IRS. Its tax year is often not the City's fiscal year, and it counts money when earned or spent under its accounting method, not when the City paid.
